plain: Each turn you pick one action from a short menu of choices, and that is your turn.
say: On your turn, pick one of these four things to do.

plain: Players compete to have the most pieces in places on the map. Whoever has the most in a place usually scores it or controls it.
say: Whoever has the most pieces in a region owns it, so try to outnumber everyone there.

plain: Players bid against each other for something, and the highest bid wins it and pays.
say: We go around and offer money for this. Raise the price or drop out, and the last one in gets it.

plain: Everyone plays on one team against the game itself. You all win together or lose together.
say: We're all on the same side tonight, and the game is trying to beat us.

plain: Everyone starts with a small, plain deck of cards and adds better cards over the game. Your deck gets stronger as you play.
say: You start with a weak pile of cards, and every turn you can buy a better one to shuffle in.

plain: Dice decide some of what happens, so luck plays a part.
say: Roll these, and the numbers tell you what you get.

plain: Players take turns picking from a shared set of options. You pick one and pass the rest along.
say: Pick one card you like and pass the rest to your left.

plain: You build up a set of things that make more stuff for you each turn, so later turns are bigger than early ones.
say: Early on, buy things that give you more things. By the end, your turns get big.

plain: Choosing well what to play, what to keep, and when, from the cards you hold.
say: These cards are your options. Think about which to use now and which to save.

plain: A game you play as a series of sessions, where the rules and pieces change for good as you go. Stickers go on the board and some cards get torn up.
say: This game changes every time we play. What we do tonight sticks for next time.

plain: You collect goods in one place and carry them to another place that wants them.
say: Grab cargo here and drop it off where someone needs it.

plain: You keep going for a bigger reward, but each step risks losing what you have built up that turn.
say: You can keep going for more, but if it goes wrong you lose this round's points. Stop whenever you like.

plain: Someone rolls dice and everyone uses the result to fill in their own sheet with a pencil.
say: Each roll, everyone picks how to use the numbers and marks it on their own sheet.

plain: You score by gathering groups of matching or related things.
say: Collect sets of the same kind. Bigger sets score more.

plain: Some players have secret roles, and the table tries to work out who is who by talking.
say: A few of us are secretly on the other side. Watch what people do and figure out who.

plain: You place tiles to build a shared map or your own area, and how they fit together matters.
say: Draw a tile and add it so it fits next to the others.

plain: Each player plays one card, and the best card wins that set of cards, called a trick. Like Spades or Hearts.
say: Everyone plays one card, and the highest card of the color that was led takes the pile.

plain: Each player has a special ability or rule that the others do not have, so everyone plays a little differently. Also called asymmetric play.
say: Your character has a special trick nobody else has. Read it and we'll see how it helps.

plain: You put one of your pieces on a spot to claim that action. Once a spot is taken, others usually cannot use it this round.
say: You get a few people. Each turn, send one to a spot on the board to do that job, and nobody else can go there this round.

plain: How many useful things you can do in a turn or a game. Extra actions are valuable.
say: Anything that lets you do one more thing on your turn is a big deal.

plain: A marker that shows who goes first. In some games it moves each round, or you can take it as an action.
say: Whoever has this goes first. It moves around as we play.

plain: One part of a round. Many games split each round into steps done in the same order every time.
say: Every round goes in the same order: first we do this, then this, then this.

plain: One full pass around the table, or one set of steps everyone does, depending on the game.
say: Once everybody has had a go, that's one round.

plain: Being a step ahead of others in timing, so you get to things first or force them to react to you.
say: Getting there first matters here, so a quick move now can beat a big move later.

plain: The order players take their turns in. Some games change it every round.
say: We go clockwise, starting with you.

plain: A housekeeping step, often at the start or end of a round, where you refresh, pay, or reset things.
say: Before the next round, we all do a little cleanup: refill this and pay for that.

plain: The face-up stack where used or thrown-away cards go.
say: Done with a card? It goes face up on this pile.

plain: The face-down stack you take new cards from. Also called the deck.
say: New cards come off the top of this stack.

plain: The most cards you can hold. If you go over, you discard down to the limit, usually at a set time.
say: You can hold up to this many cards. Any extra go back.

plain: Throwing back your starting hand and drawing a new one, sometimes with a small cost.
say: Don't like your first hand? You can swap it once.

plain: The cards you have played in front of you, which stay out and usually help you for the rest of the game.
say: Cards you play stay in front of you and keep helping you.

plain: Turning a card sideways to show you have used it. It comes back at a set time, often your next turn.
say: Turn this card sideways once you've used it. It's ready again next turn.

plain: The thing that starts the end of the game, like a track filling up or a pile running out. Often play finishes the round after it.
say: When someone reaches this, we finish the round and then count up.

plain: When a player who cannot win still decides who does, by choosing whom to help or hurt.
say: If you can't win, it's fine to just play your best move. Nobody has to pick the winner.

plain: A game where almost everything you do scores a few points in a different way, so there are many paths to win.
say: Nearly everything here gets you points, so do what looks fun and you'll score.

plain: A player who gets ahead early and keeps getting further ahead, because being ahead makes it easier to stay ahead.
say: If someone pulls way ahead, it's worth teaming up to slow them down.

plain: The rule that decides the winner when scores are equal. It differs from game to game.
say: If we tie, the one with more of these wins.

plain: The points that decide who wins. Most points at the end wins.
say: Whoever has the most points at the end wins. These are the points.

plain: A game built around story, theme, and drama, often with dice, fighting, and big swings. Ameritrash is an old hobby nickname; thematic game is the kinder term.
say: This one is about the story, so expect big moments, lucky rolls, and some chaos.

plain: When a player gets stuck thinking about a move for a long time because there are so many options. Often shortened to AP.
say: Take your time. If it helps, tell me the two moves you're stuck between.

plain: BoardGameGeek, a large website with a database of board games, forums, and ratings.
say: There's a big website where people rate games, if you want to find more like this one.

plain: A style of game, first popular in Germany, with little luck, little direct conflict, and many ways to score points.
say: Nobody attacks anybody in this one. We're each building our own thing and comparing points at the end.

plain: Friendly local game store, the hobby shop where people buy and often play games.
say: There's a game shop nearby where you can try games before you buy them.

plain: A game that is easy to learn and fun for new players, often someone's first modern board game.
say: This one's quick to learn, and it's a nice first step into newer games.

plain: A change to the official rules that a group agrees to use at their table.
say: The book says one thing, but tonight let's play it this way. Everyone okay with that?

plain: A small wooden person-shaped playing piece. The word blends my and people.
say: These little wooden people are your pieces.

plain: In a team game, one player who tells everyone else what to do on their turns.
say: We can all share ideas, but on your turn, you make the call.

plain: A player who holds the table closely to the exact rules, sometimes more than the moment needs.
say: Let's play it this way for now and check the book after the game.

plain: Moves that directly hurt another player, like stealing from them or wrecking their plans.
say: Some cards let you mess with other people. It's part of the fun, not personal.

plain: How complex or heavy a game is to learn and play. A light game is simple; a heavy game has many rules and long turns.
say: This one's on the lighter side, so we'll be playing in a few minutes.
